title: For Reinsurers, Disciplined Growth Takes Center Stage
gist: Reinsurance TSR decelerated from 29% in 2024 to 14% in 2025 as the hard-market tailwind fades, while dedicated global reinsurance capital hit $648 billion (up 11%) at end-2025. With P&C reinsurers running a ~94% combined ratio and only ~7 of 16 points of RoTE coming from underwriting, BCG argues the next phase of value creation depends on saying no to business rather than growing premium.

insights.claim: Reinsurance one-year total shareholder return decelerated sharply from 29% in 2024 to 14% in 2025, versus a 19.1% average annual TSR over the five years through 2025.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The hard-market repricing trade in reinsurance equities is largely spent; expect multiple compression risk if 2026 returns keep normalizing toward the 13.4% ten-year average.
insights.quote: one-year TSR decelerated sharply from 29% in 2024 to 14% in 2025
insights.locator: The reinsurance industry is at an inflection point

insights.claim: Even at a decelerating 14%, reinsurance's 2025 TSR remained above its 10-year average annual TSR of 13.4%, so the sector still screens as a long-term compounder rather than a broken one.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Frames the deceleration as normalization, not a cycle break — argues for selectivity within the sector rather than wholesale de-rating.
insights.locator: That 14% TSR is still above the 10-year average

insights.claim: Capital abundance, not scarcity, is the binding constraint for reinsurers: dedicated global reinsurance capital reached an estimated $648 billion at end-2025 (up 11% year over year, per Gallagher Re), while tangible book value across a 12-reinsurer sample grew from $119 billion at YE2022 to $162 billion at YE2025, an 11% annual rate.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Double-digit capital growth on both sides implies pricing pressure at upcoming renewals — watch for softening rate-on-line and use it as the leading indicator for underwriting margin compression.
insights.locator: Across the 12 reinsurers in our extended sample

insights.claim: P&C reinsurance averaged a 16% return on tangible equity over 2021-2025, but only about 7 percentage points came from underwriting versus 9 percentage points from investment returns, on a 66% loss ratio and 28% expense ratio equal to a 94% combined ratio.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Over half of reinsurer RoTE is rate-sensitive investment income, so a rate-cut cycle plus softening pricing hits the P&L twice — stress-test names whose returns lean on the investment leg.
insights.quote: an average 16% return on tangible equity (RoTE), comprising approximately 7 percentage points from underwriting and 9 percentage points from investment returns
insights.locator: For 2021-2025, our P&C reinsurance benchmarking analysis

insights.claim: With only six points of underwriting margin inside a 94% combined ratio, a relatively small change in pricing or loss experience produces a disproportionate hit to reinsurance underwriting returns.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Reinsurer earnings are convex to softening: model downside on a few points of rate decline, not a linear glide path.
insights.quote: There isn’t unlimited underwriting margin available to absorb price deterioration.
insights.locator: The underlying economics include an average 66% loss ratio

insights.claim: The decomposition of shareholder value into tangible book value growth, price-to-tangible-book multiple change, and cash-flow contribution shows cash-flow contribution (dividends and share-count change) was the largest component of reinsurance's 13.4% ten-year annual TSR, with value creation becoming more balanced over the most recent five years.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Buybacks and dividends historically drove reinsurer returns more than book growth — favor management teams willing to return capital when deployment opportunities thin out.
insights.locator: BCG’s TSR methodology helps explain why

themes.theme: Discipline, quality of earnings, and named outperformers

insights.claim: Munich Re, Arch Capital, and Hannover Re stand out over a ten-year analysis for combining relatively high average annual TSR with comparatively low volatility of annual shareholder returns, though the five-year picture is more varied.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A concrete watchlist of franchises whose underwriting discipline has already shown up as low-volatility compounding — the profile most likely to hold up as pricing softens.
insights.locator: Our long-term shareholder-return analysis provides some evidence

insights.claim: Because two reinsurers can report similar headline returns while differing in underwriting performance, investment contribution, reserve development, and catastrophe experience, investors will increasingly price repeatability of earnings rather than the level of returns.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Expect valuation dispersion by earnings quality — screen reserve development and cat load rather than trusting headline RoTE or combined ratio.
insights.quote: Investors are therefore likely to pay increasing attention not just to the level of returns, but to how repeatable those returns are throughout the cycle.
insights.locator: The challenge now is not simply to preserve profitability

insights.claim: In an abundant-capital reinsurance market the decisive skill is declining business rather than winning it, so premium growth is the wrong success metric and value-accretive growth is the right one.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Treat shrinking premium volume at a disciplined reinsurer as a bullish signal, and aggressive top-line growth into a softening market as a red flag.
insights.quote: In a market where capacity is abundant and pricing is under pressure, sometimes the most value-creating decision is to say no.
insights.locator: The next few years will not test who can deploy the most capital

insights.claim: AI is generating new, highly correlated risks for reinsurers — specifically data centers and business interruption — that stack on top of geopolitical and climate exposures just as underwriting margin thins.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Correlated AI-infrastructure exposure undercuts the diversification assumption behind reinsurer capital models; watch data-center and cyber/BI aggregation disclosures.
insights.quote: new, highly correlated risks emerging from AI, such as data centers and business interruption
insights.locator: All that will be put to the test given the current geopolitical landscape
